content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To clean combat boots, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Remove the nylon laces (1 minute)
Step 2. Apply a second layer of edge dressing to the soles (10 minutes)
Step 3. Fill a basin with lukewarm water and mild soap (2 minutes)
Step 4. Buff the toe cap to a mirror shine (15 minutes)
Step 5. Spray boots with a water-repellent finish (5 minutes)
Step 6. Scrub the exterior leather with a soft brush (8 minutes)
Step 7. Insert cedar shoe trees to maintain shape (30 seconds)
Step 8. Purchase a heavy-duty stiff-bristled mud brush (15 minutes)
Step 9. Wipe away excess moisture with a microfiber cloth (3 minutes)
Step 10. Apply a thin layer of mink oil for conditioning (12 minutes)
Step 11. Shake out any loose debris from inside the boots (30 seconds)
Step 12. Organize your cleaning workstation (5 minutes)
Step 13. Polish the heel counter with a circular motion (10 minutes)
Step 14. Clean the metal eyelets with a cotton swab (6 minutes)
Step 15. Soak the laces in soapy water (20 minutes)
Step 16. Remove stubborn scuff marks with a gum eraser (4 minutes)
Step 17. Use a toothpick to clear dirt from the stitching (10 minutes)
Step 18. Inspect the boots for structural damage (3 minutes)
Step 19. Apply a base coat of black wax polish (15 minutes)
Step 20. Disinfect the interior with an antifungal spray (2 minutes)
Step 21. Use a damp cloth to remove fine dust (4 minutes)
Step 22. Lay out a protective newspaper or mat (2 minutes)
Step 23. Check the tread for trapped stones or gravel (5 minutes)
Step 24. Rinse the laces under cold running water (2 minutes)
Step 25. Knock the soles together to loosen dried mud (30 seconds)
Step 26. Prepare a specialized leather cleaner solution (3 minutes)
Step 27. Hang the laces to air dry completely (4 hours)
Step 28. Gather a set of soft polishing cloths (2 minutes)
Step 29. Apply a high-pigment cream to faded areas (10 minutes)
Step 30. Use a horsehair brush to buff the cream (5 minutes)
Step 31. Thread the dried laces back through the eyelets (5 minutes)
Step 32. Scrape heavy mud off the outsoles (10 minutes)
Step 33. Let the wax polish cure (30 minutes)
Step 34. Brush off dried mud from the boot tongue (5 minutes)
Step 35. Soften the leather with a handheld steamer (3 minutes)
Step 36. Remove the insoles for separate cleaning (1 minute)
Step 37. Mix a solution for deep-cleaning the soles (4 minutes)
Step 38. Acquire a tin of high-quality boot wax (20 minutes)
Step 39. Buff the entire boot with a clean cloth (8 minutes)
Step 40. Deodorize the insoles with baking soda (1 hour)
Step 41. Apply a leather preservative to the welt (7 minutes)
Step 42. Scrub the gusseted tongue area (6 minutes)
Step 43. Tap the boots to ensure all loose sand is out (1 minute)
Step 44. Heat the wax polish slightly for better absorption (2 minutes)
Step 45. Apply a matte finish to the rubber side-walls (5 minutes)
Step 46. Locate a specialized suede brush for the ankle collar (5 minutes)
Step 47. Clean the transition line between sole and upper (8 minutes)
Step 48. Wipe the interior leather lining (5 minutes)
Step 49. Brush the seams with a small nylon brush (4 minutes)
Step 50. Apply a UV protectant to the synthetic panels (6 minutes)
Step 51. Allow the boots to air dry away from direct heat (6 hours)
Step 52. Inspect the outsoles for even wear (2 minutes)
Step 53. Condition the leather pull-loops (3 minutes)
Step 54. Wipe off any excess polish from the eyelets (4 minutes)
Step 55. Adjust the tongue for a centered fit (30 seconds)
Step 56. Re-insert the cleaned insoles (1 minute)
Step 57. Seal the edges of the leather (5 minutes)
Step 58. Final inspection of the toe box (2 minutes)
Step 59. Gather various grades of sandpaper for sole repair (10 minutes)
Step 60. Apply edge dressing to the sides of the soles (10 minutes)
Step 61. Hand-rub the leather to generate heat and shine (12 minutes)
Step 62. Brush the ankle collar to restore nap (4 minutes)
Step 63. Wash the boot exterior with a damp sponge (7 minutes)
Step 64. Use a welt brush to clean the stitching grooves (6 minutes)
Step 65. Set up a fan to improve air circulation (2 minutes)
Step 66. Wipe the boot hardware with a dry cloth (3 minutes)
Step 67. Deep clean the crevices of the lug soles (15 minutes)
Step 68. Rinse the exterior soap residue (3 minutes)
Step 69. Clean the work surface of any spilled polish (5 minutes)
Step 70. Use a stiff brush on the tread patterns (8 minutes)
Step 71. Vacuum the interior of the boots (3 minutes)
Step 72. Prepare a "spit-shine" water cup (1 minute)
Step 73. Clear a space on a sturdy workbench (5 minutes)
Step 74. Check the condition of the lace aglets (1 minute)
Step 75. Inventory your cleaning supplies (5 minutes)
Step 76. Air out the boots in a cool, dry place (2 hours)
Step 77. Buff the boots with a final lint-free cloth (5 minutes)
Step 78. Let the conditioning oil soak in (1 hour)
Step 79. Sand down any rough spots on the sole edges (5 minutes)
Step 80. Wipe the polish tin rim to prevent sticking (1 minute)
Step 81. Apply a second coat of wax to the heel (10 minutes)
Step 82. Store the boots in a breathable dust bag (2 minutes)
Step 83. Remove old wax buildup with a solvent (10 minutes)
Step 84. Read the manufacturer's care instructions (5 minutes)
Step 85. Clean the junction where the sole meets the heel (6 minutes)
Step 86. Apply a waterproofing wax to the seams (8 minutes)
Step 87. Polish the metal speed-hooks (5 minutes)
Step 88. Check for any loose threads on the uppers (2 minutes)
Step 89. Prepare a mild degreasing solution (3 minutes)
Step 90. Take a photo of the refurbished boots (1 minute)
